subject.title: Add a retraction window for forwarded exec approvals (agent-cancellable hold before prompt delivery)

question: Should OpenClaw add an opt-in agent-cancellable hold window for forwarded exec approvals, and if so what core protocol/config boundary should own retraction?
rationale: The request changes approval timing, auditability, Gateway RPC shape, and Codex/native command-approval semantics; code inspection can confirm the gap but cannot choose the safe product contract.

options.title: Design default-off core hold/retract
options.body: Add an additive `approvals.exec` hold setting and explicit retraction RPC only after specifying fail-open delivery, fail-closed execution, audit, docs, and compatibility tests.

options.title: Keep immediate forwarding
options.body: Reject retraction and instead rely on existing allowlists, safe-bin policy, and approval routing so every prompt reaches the human as soon as it is created.

options.title: Defer behind narrower approval cleanup
options.body: Leave this open until existing duplicate/noisy approval issues are reduced, then revisit whether a hold window is still needed.

recommendation.title: Design default-off core hold/retract
recommendation.body: Add an additive `approvals.exec` hold setting and explicit retraction RPC only after specifying fail-open delivery, fail-closed execution, audit, docs, and compatibility tests.

likelyOwner.reason: He has the broadest history across the approval safety, forwarding, and Gateway protocol paths and merged the original forwarding work.
